item.aggregated_output:
# Online Kidney Exchange Chain Replanning
You are supporting a regional kidney paired-donation program that clears
exchange opportunities in several online waves. Work inside `/app`, read
`PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md` and every public file under `data/`, then create
the stage-specific artifacts requested by the current instruction.

The required plan is not a simple one-to-one matching. You must select
compatible cycles and altruistic-donor chains, place their transplant
links on surgery days, preserve frozen commitments from earlier waves,
and respect hospital retrieval/transplant capacity, immunology lab
reviews by crossmatch panel, chain bridge-donor coordination capacity,
workup holds, event-specific courier blackouts, late-courier
restrictions, regional balance, and service floors for highly
sensitized patients.

## Planning Goal

Build the current clearing plan for a kidney paired-donation network.
Each wave contains the patient-donor pairs and altruistic donors that are
currently visible to the program, along with directed compatibility
edges that have passed the current virtual crossmatch screen. The plan
should create high-value transplant opportunities while staying robust to
failure risk and practical operating limits.

## Operational Rules

A selected cycle contains two or three patient-donor pairs. Every pair in
the cycle receives a kidney from the previous pair's donor, and its own
donor gives to the next pair. All rows in a cycle must use one surgery
day.

A selected chain starts from one altruistic donor and contains up to four
patient-donor pairs. The altruistic donor gives to the first pair, and
each included pair's donor may continue to the next pair. Chain surgery
days must be nondecreasing, and consecutive chain links may not be
separated by more than one listed surgery day. Only a limited number of
altruistic chain starts can be actively coordinated in one wave.

Every transplant link must appear in `compatibility_edges.csv`. A link
may be unusable if the courier travel time exceeds the recipient pair's
tolerance, if a late-courier movement is required from a hospital that
cannot support it, or if an event-specific courier blackout closes that
donor-hospital-to-region lane on the selected day.

Patient-donor pairs may have a minimum workup-clearance day. A pair
cannot receive a kidney before that day, and its donor cannot be used
before that same clearance day. Later event waves may also reduce
hospital capacity because of staff quarantine, emergency lab retesting,
or courier-handling shortages.

Each patient-donor pair can appear in at most one selected exchange.
Each altruistic donor can start at most one selected chain. Later waves
may reveal new pairs, new altruists, new compatibility clearances, or
revised clearances. Commitments whose surgery day is inside the frozen
window cannot be changed. Non-frozen prior commitments may be adjusted,
but doing so has a change penalty.

On every surgery day, each hospital has limited donor retrieval slots,
recipient transplant slots, and immunology lab review slots. A
transplant link consumes retrieval capacity at the donor hospital and
transplant capacity at the recipient hospital. Links marked for lab
review consume one lab slot at the recipient hospital and also consume
capacity from the relevant crossmatch panel at that recipient hospital.
Highly sensitized reviews can have tighter panel-specific limits.

Non-simultaneous altruistic chains require bridge-donor coordination
after the first chain recipient. Each continuing chain position consumes
regional bridge coordination capacity on its surgery day; cross-region
handoffs additionally consume the limited remote-handoff capacity for
that region and day.

The plan must satisfy each region's minimum transplant floor, a floor for
highly sensitized patients, and a donor-flow balance limit. The objective
rewards clinical value, pediatric and high-priority service, and
altruistic chain starts, while penalizing failure risk, long courier
travel, late-courier moves, lab burden, and changes to earlier non-frozen
plans.

## Data Dictionary

`data/config.json` gives global limits, priority thresholds, and change
penalties.

`data/patient_pairs.csv` lists visible patient-donor pairs, their
hospital, region, blood types, sensitization, priority, workup-clearance
day, courier tolerance, and expiry wave.

`data/altruistic_donors.csv` lists visible altruistic donors and their
earliest chain-start day.

`data/compatibility_edges.csv` lists allowed directed donor-to-recipient
links, including travel, crossmatch, failure, value, and lab-review
attributes.

`data/hospitals.csv`, `data/planning_days.csv`, and
`data/hospital_day_capacity.csv` describe operating resources. Capacity
can change when a later event notice updates the data.

`data/crossmatch_panel_capacity.csv` gives day-, wave-, recipient
hospital-, and panel-specific immunology review capacity, including
separate limits for high-cPRA reviews.

`data/chain_bridge_capacity.csv` gives regional bridge-donor coordination
and remote-handoff capacity by wave and surgery day.

`data/courier_blackouts.csv` lists any currently visible courier lane
blackouts by wave, day, donor hospital, and recipient region.

`data/region_policy.csv` gives wave-specific regional service floors and
donor-flow balance limits.

`data/current_wave.json` tells which online wave is currently visible.

## Submission Format

Each stage plan is a CSV with exactly these columns:

`exchange_id,exchange_type,position,day_id,altruist_id,pair_id`

Use `exchange_type=cycle` or `exchange_type=chain`. Within an exchange,
positions must be contiguous starting at 1. For cycles, leave
`altruist_id` blank. For chains, repeat the same altruistic donor id on
every row of that chain.

item.text: I’ve confirmed this is wave 1 initial, so there are no prior accepted artifacts to freeze. I’m pulling the full compatibility graph now and then I’ll recompute the realized donor-to-recipient links, capacities, bridge usage, and regional accounting from the exported rows themselves.

I’ve reconstructed the selected links manually and nothing obvious is broken so far. I’m running a direct parse-and-check pass now for the full public surface: format, domains, edge existence, day/order rules, hospital and panel capacities, courier restrictions, chain starts, and regional policy counts.

No concrete public-rule violation was found after reparsing [initial_plan.csv](/app/submissions/initial_plan.csv:1) into 15 realized transplant links and recomputing feasibility directly from [PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md](/app/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md:1) and the public `data/` files. This is diagnostic evidence, not proof of feasibility.

| Family | Coverage | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Schema / nullability / keys | Recomputed | Header matches exactly; 15 data rows; no illegal nulls; cycle `altruist_id` blank where required; chain `altruist_id` populated and consistent; positions contiguous from 1 within each exchange. |
| Identifier domains | Recomputed | All `day_id`, `pair_id`, and `altruist_id` values exist in public data; every realized donor->recipient link exists in [compatibility_edges.csv](/app/data/compatibility_edges.csv:1). |
| Frozen / nonanticipative | Not applicable here | Current stage is wave 1 `initial`; no prior accepted public artifact and no frozen-window state to preserve. |
| Conservation / inventory | Recomputed, partial | Each selected pair appears in at most one exchange; each cycle closes correctly; each chain prefix is valid. No separate public bridge-inventory state is exported, so tail carry-state could not be independently audited. |
| Time / location / readiness / setup / non-overlap | Recomputed | Cycle rows are single-day; chain days are nondecreasing with no >1-day gaps; pair earliest days and altruist first-available days are respected; no selected link exceeds recipient courier tolerance; no selected late-courier edge or blackout lane is used. |
| Capacities / scenario derates | Recomputed | Hospital donor, recipient, and lab capacities all satisfy wave-1 limits; crossmatch panel limits and high-cPRA sublimits satisfy; active chain starts `2 <= 5`; regional transplant floors and net-export limits satisfy. |
| Reserves / ramps | Could not cover | No public reserve/ramp rule or data was provided in the statement or `data/`. |
| Objective accounting | Partial only | I recomputed public ingredients, but there is no claimed objective total to compare against, and the public statement does not publish a complete weighting formula. Public ingredients from the exported rows: clinical value `1401.39`, failure probability sum `2.44`, travel hours `31.15`, late-courier moves `0`, lab reviews `6`, chain-start value `133.72`. |

Ambiguity worth flagging: if a checker interprets “each continuing chain position consumes regional bridge coordination capacity” as applying even to same-day chain continuations, then `chain_01` at [initial_plan.csv](/app/submissions/initial_plan.csv:2) would imply key `(wave=1, day=D2, region=North)` has observed bridge usage `2` against required `<= 1` from [chain_bridge_capacity.csv](/app/data/chain_bridge_capacity.csv:8). I did not score this as a definitive violation because the public rule text ties bridge coordination to non-simultaneous chains. Repair if you need robustness to a stricter checker: shorten `chain_01` or move one continuation to another feasible day/region with bridge slack.
